title: I Posted the Calliope-Whistle Hours After They Camped My Numbered Keyboard

parts.text: I stepped into the fair wagon at 11:04 a.m. and host Bette was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE WAGON. SIXTY MINUTES. WHISTLES STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was thirty-two, fair secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered whistles. Bette shrugged. "Hosts are the steam." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover valves on my numbered keyboard. Then I asked for the whistle log. At 11:12 the lot pinged why Bette's name was on my valves. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The lot can see Bette's leftover valves on my numbered keyboard.

social.video_title: They camped my numbered calliope keyboard — Part 1/2
social.description: Fair wagon, leftover valves, a sixty-minute clock she posted. I logged the whistles. Would you have asked for the whistle log?

parts.text: Bette called it steam-up until the lot asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the valve still. The keyboard went back to my numbered slot. Bette ran a slot of her own and told the next host atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: HOSTS ARE NOT THE STEAM. I keep my whistles on a labeled rack. Bette brown-bags her steam-ups. The wagon finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Hosts are not the steam — Part 2/2
social.description: Whistle log, numbered keyboard, and a second line on the board. Was steam-up ever my valves?
